lines.text: I had read two books about ships. Neither of them mentioned that the sea goes up and down. For four days.
Cheer up, my lord. You've gone a lovely shade of green. Very fashionable in Vask.
Vask was the first city I had ever seen where nobody asked how many rings I had. They only asked what I had to sell.
My counting house. My warehouses. My two ships. At the next quarter-day, Lady Sabine takes all of them. I owe eleven thousand crowns. She paid twenty-two thousand for the pleasure of collecting it.
We don't have eleven thousand crowns.
We have something better.
We rented a vault on the Exchange canal and filled it with Deep rimeglass. Then Pell invited every merchant in Vask to come and look.
Every note we print says Greyhollow will pay the bearer in rimeglass. And there's the rimeglass. Bring a lamp if you don't believe me. You won't need it.
In Vask, anyone may open a counting house. Even a lord with no rings. We only ask one thing. Is the glass real?
It was real. And none of it had a shape inside. That was Skeld law now, and mine.
By the end of the week, merchants were buying Greyhollow notes faster than the printer could dry them.
Pell Marrow's debts. Eleven thousand crowns. Paid in full.
Lady Sabine wants the ships, my lord, not your paper. I refuse your payment.
In Vask, sir, a debt offered in full is a debt paid. Refuse it, and you have simply given it away.
He signed. Lady Sabine had paid twice what Pell's debts were worth. We had paid exactly what they were worth. By law, she had to take it.
My ships. My house. My good name, such as it was. And now I owe all of it to you, my lord.
So why should I trust a merchant who owes me eleven thousand crowns?
Loyal to profit, my lord. And you're very profitable.
So the Greyhollow counting house opened its doors in Vask, under Pell's old roof. Pell said it was the first bank in the world built on glass. For once, I didn't check.
In Corrow, Lady Sabine read her factor's letter twice. Then she closed her fan.
Clever boy.
When we sailed back into Saltmouth, another letter from Bram was waiting on the dock. Also one line.
Come home. Tobin has built something.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter forty-seven, coming soon.
